                                                      Abstract
           We introduce moonowers, a weaker analogue of sunowers. A family of sets S1 , . . . , Sk is a
       k -moonower if each set Si contains at least one element that is absent from all the others. We
       study the extremal problem of determining the largest possible size of a family of sets of size at
       most w that avoids a k-moonower, and obtain near-optimal bounds.
          As an application, we revisit the code sparsication problem studied by Brakensiek and
       Guruswami (STOC 2025) and improve the bounds to near optimal. Concretely, we improve
       the dependence on the block length from poly-logarithmic to logarithmic, and show that such a
       dependence is necessary.

1.1 Moonowers

       It is easy to see that a sunower is either a moonower or becomes one after removing one set .
